# Review pass 1 — kebra-nagast-ch67

Reviewer: adversarial pass 1. Read: conventions.md, runbook.md, packet.md, units.json, known-forms.json, novel-forms.json. No modern translations; Dillmann unavailable, so every lexical call below is hedged (?). `t` untouched (verified: all 38 `t` and `p` flags identical to the draft; joined `t` equals the packet Geʿez); units.json parses; schema unchanged (t, l, i, n, p).

Overall: grammar labels were mostly sound. The faults were (a) one garbled `i` (unit 15), (b) `l`/`i` mismatches and `l` lines that were not word-by-word, (c) lexical calls stated without a hedge, (d) a few wrong labels or lemmas in notes.

## Allusions checked

Kept as drafted (confident): 1 Kings 11:1–8 (unit 3); Psalm 143:2, Job 4:17 (4); Psalm 7:9, Jeremiah 17:10 (5); Prayer of Manasseh 8 (9); Psalm 132:10, 1 Kings 11:12–13 (10); 1 Corinthians 1:20–27 (12); Deuteronomy 17:17, 7:3–4 (17); 1 Kings 12 (21); Genesis 37, 41–47, 45:10 (23); Exodus 12–14, 7–12, 14:16/21, 16 (29–33); Deuteronomy 8:4 (34); Deuteronomy 7:1, Revelation 12:3 (?) (36); Revelation 20:3 (37); Isaiah 2:2, Micah 4:1 (38). Psalm 107:16 (31) kept as "compare". 1 Cor 1:25 (19) softened to "echoes". No allusion removed.

## Drafter's flagged units

2 (done, 1–2); 13 (note already hedges; no change, meanings of መያጤ/ዐሳዬ stay inferred); 14 (hedged "wiped (?)" already; no change); 19 (26–28); 20 (29); 21 (reading as 3ms confirmed by ይሤርዎሙ with singular subject in 37; no change; identification left open); 24 (33); 30 (checked: ዐሠርተ, ፲, ለሕይወት, Exodus 7–12 all fine; no change); 33 (42); 35 (checked: ኢየሱስ = Joshua (Ἰησοῦς in the Greek Bible), ገነተ ትፍሥሕት fine; no change).

## Findings refused / left alone

- Proper names in `l`: conventions say "Geʿez form in `l`", yet `l` carries English forms (Solomon, Israel, Joshua…) throughout, as the pilot model presumably does. I could not verify against the pilot (not in my reading list) and did not mass-convert. Orchestrator should confirm against kebra-nagast-ch1.json; if Geʿez is wanted, one scripted pass over `l` fixes it.
- Unit 5 `l` "kidneys" vs `i` "inner parts": legitimate idiom, note explains; left.
- Unit 14 "wipe (?)" and unit 13 inferred meanings: already hedged by the drafter; left.
- Unit 9 "since" for ሶበ + perfect: defensible and noted by the drafter; left.
- Unit 17 "The chief of the evil is that…": elliptical Geʿez, `i` is a fair smoothing; left.
- Gloss files: known-forms entries ለእከይ ("restating the object of አብዝኃ") and ተሐትት ("she asks", 3fs) do not fit this chapter (ተሐትት here is 2ms, ለእከይ is a possessor after ርእሳ); the glosser should broaden/correct them. Not an edit to units.json.

- ሐጸ, ዘይሴወር, ፅዉስ, አረፍት, ነሰተ (ይነስት), ነቅዐ, ግብርና/ግብርናት, ተርባነ, አስተሐቀረ (base ሐቀረ), ሣቀየ spelling: lemma or sense cannot be confirmed without Dillmann. Each is already hedged (?) in the entry; I did not replace them with other guesses.
- No change of the translation-wide `i` beyond the above: a re-read of all 38 units against `l` and the text found no further omission, added word or mislabelled grammar in the notes (checked 3ms/3fs/3mp, -ኦ/-ሙ/-ክሙ suffixes, construct chains, gerunds and infinitives).
- Proper names in `l` (Geʿez vs English) remain as in pass 1: orchestrator to confirm against kebra-nagast-ch1.json.
- Unit 29 note calls ግብርናት an "abstract plural": the form could instead be a singular abstract in -ት; unverifiable here, left (the gloss is hedged).
